name: Many Peaks, Mt Marlow and the Wetlands
description:
Sun, 23rd July 2023
 
Town Common Conservation Park
Shelly Beach, Many Peaks, Mt Marlow
Leader: Wendy Williams 

Rated: Easy-Medium. On-Track. Good for beginner level bushwalkers who can do a 5 hour walk. Moderate level of fitness is required. 

Walk Description:

We might change the plan on the day - but the general gist of the plan is to take advantage of the lowtide and make our way around Pallarenda to Shelly Beach, then along the Towns Common Trail up to M from the Northern end to finish up at Cape Pallarenda

Approximate Time/Distance: 6 hours return (including breaks), 20 ish kms

What to bring:

Sunscreen and hat
Insect repellent
Shoes appropriate for walking on rocky, uneven surfaces
Morning tea & trail snacks
Water (I would recommend a minimum of 3 litres for this walk)
Camera
First aid kit/snake bite kit
Long pants or gaitors for the short-cuts we might choose to take to explore.
 

Meeting point: End of Cape Pallarenda Rd, near the old Quarantine Station buildings and the footbridge that goes over the creek at 7:00 am - see map pin.

Information and maps for the Townsville Town Common Conservation Park:
https://wanderstories.space/cape-pallarenda/
https://parks.des.qld.gov.au/parks/townsville/

name: The Short Way to the Pub, Maggie Island
description:
Sun, 16th July 2023

The short way to the Pub
Magnetic Island - Nelly to Horseshoe Bay via the ridge and Bays 
Leader: Cherry Judge

Rated: On-Track hike. For moderately fit  walkers who can walk at a reasonably steady pace for a 6-ish hr hike.  

Meeting: Meet at 6:00 am Sealink Ferry Terminal to catch the 6:30 am Ferry. Locals, please bring id (license, utilities bill, if no license) as locals get a discount on the fare.

Walk Description:

Beginning at the ferry terminal in Nelly Bay, we’ll make our way along Mandalay Avenue up the ridge, and then follow the ridge track towards the Forts junction. From here, we'll do part of the five bays trail, checking out a couple of lookouts and an old searchlight station; before arriving at Florence Bay for a decent break. From Florence Bay, we will continue over the ridge to Horseshoe Bay.

Once in Horseshoe Bay, we could have a few drinks here and find a place to have lunch. I was thinking of catching the bus and heading to Scallywags to have lunch there if they are open [ I shall check] - Otherwise we could have lunch in Horsehoe Bay itself [ somewhere other than the pub- the wait is incredibly long the last few times we went]

If you're not familiar with Magnetic Island, the following links should assist:
https://wanderstories.space/what-to-see-on-magnetic-island/
https://www.npsr.qld.gov.au/parks/magnetic-island/pdf/magnetic-island-map.pdf   

What to expect:
Moderate grade hike. Approximate distance/duration: 13kms, 5 hours.

Moderate level of fitness required. Expect some steep and uneven sections - you will need to be comfortable with hills! There are exposed sections, so expect it to be hot in places. The pace will be moderate and continuous, so we can cover the distance within the designated time-frame and enjoy our stops.

What to bring:
-Water (3 Litres minimum)
-A hat and sunscreen
-Insect repellent
-Trail snacks and morning tea
-Shoes appropriate for walking on rocky, uneven surfaces
-Dry clothes and perhaps a pair of thongs for after the walk
-First aid kit/snake bite kit.
-Ginger/motion sickness tablets for the ferry if you get seasick
-Petty cash for bus and shops

name: Lower Ethel Creek & Falls
description:
Sat, 8th July 2023
Ethel Creek Falls +  
Leader: Ian Wallace

Rated: On-Track hike. For the easy to moderately fit walkers who can walk about 4-5 hrs.
Off-Track component [optional] - For the more adventurous - After reaching Ethel Creek Falls, we will explore the lower reaches of Ethel creek (Creek hopping). Those that are not keen to do that can spend longer at the Falls and have a leisurely picnic and wait for the group to return.   

Meeting: Meet at 6:30 am at Yabulu Service station.  You will be meeting Ian Wallace there.  

Walk Description:

We will begin in Paluma village, making our way to Cloudy Creek.
Once we reach Cloudy Creek, we will cross the creek and then continue along a 'less traveled' track to Ethel Creek Falls.
We stop for morning tea and a swim at Ethel creek Falls.
For those that are keen to follow Ian - he will be exploring further down Ethel Creek - rock hopping, creek walking for an hour or so and then turn back to join those that are enjoying an extended swim at the falls. Then we come back the same way

The full hike will be around 13 kms. We am allowing 7 hours. If you are not interested in exploring the lower reaches of Ethel creek with Ian, bring a book to enjoy the solitude as you wait for the group to return. We would not want anyone to head back to the start point alone. We stay with the group please.

Have a read of the Wanderstories blog if you would like more info about the area: https://wanderstories.space/ethel-creek-falls/

What to bring:
-Water (3 Litres minimum)
-A hat and sunscreen
-Insect repellent
-Trail snacks and morning tea
-Shoes appropriate for walking on rocky, uneven surfaces
-Dry clothes and perhaps a pair of thongs for after the walk
-First aid kit/snake bite kit.
- Swimmers , if swimming
